stops.note: named the cane or reed fence used to build raised agricultural plots in shallow lakes
stops.meaning: a fence of reeds or canes

stops.note: adopted into Mexican Spanish to describe the Aztec raised-bed farming system
borrowed into English through historical and archaeological writing on Aztec agriculture
stops.meaning: a Mesoamerican raised-field farming technique, sometimes called a 'floating garden'

current_meaning: an artificial agricultural island built in shallow lake beds, developed by the Aztecs and still used in parts of Mexico
